sn12.35:5.1: “Twist” (_visūka_) is used with “dodge” (_vipphandita_) and sometimes “duck” (_visevita_) for an horse fighting the bit ([mn65:33.2]()) or a crab escaping the torment of children ([mn35:23.9]()). _Visūka_ is also used for a “show” of dance, etc., where the commentarial gloss _paṭāṇi_ (“screw”) reinforces the sense “twist, gyrate”. As descriptions of views, they suggest the active process of denial and distortion through which views shape how we see the world.
